reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent static review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP (retail PE view_1), radare2 6.2.0 CFG and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe; candidate source read from this worktree. No game process was executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.
review_basis: Retail 0x004B8C10 was re-disassembled, re-decompiled and re-CFG'd through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered with radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast. The candidate is scripts/GameNatives/break/004B8C10-BreakScript.cpp at sha256 153030b8cd811796440dd05dd495d6ae4e98958ca3e0354391a8797ed402634b (recorded implementation.signature: int32_t BreakScript(int32_t param_1);). The evidence artifact digests are bound in this review.

retail_function.name: BreakScript
retail_function.summary: Single block 0x4B8C10-0x4B8C55: store 1 to g_a965A4, build the 24-byte record {0,?,0,0,0x567C74,?} on the stack, `rep movsd` 6 dwords to the result buffer read from [E+4], and return that buffer pointer.

candidate_function.summary: Break_Script(int context) sets g_a965a4=1, initialises item_18/item_10/item_c to 0 and item_8 to &g_567C74, memcpys 0x18 bytes from &item_18 to `context`, and returns `context`.

candidate_comparison.statement: No candidate divergence found in the checked dimensions.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.detail: Retail entry 0x004B8C10 is recovered by all three tools; the address-bound implementation is scripts/GameNatives/break/004B8C10-BreakScript.cpp (sha256 153030b8cd811796440dd05dd495d6ae4e98958ca3e0354391a8797ed402634b). Single block 0x4B8C10-0x4B8C55: store 1 to g_a965A4, build the 24-byte record {0,?,0,0,0x567C74,?} on the stack, `rep movsd` 6 dwords to the result buffer read from [E+4], and return that buffer pointer. Candidate: Break_Script(int context) sets g_a965a4=1, initialises item_18/item_10/item_c to 0 and item_8 to &g_567C74, memcpys 0x18 bytes from &item_18 to `context`, and returns `context`.

checks.name: abi_and_signature
checks.detail: BN models `int32_t(int32_t arg1)`; retail reads the single result buffer from [E+4], which is the candidate's cdecl `context` slot. The one-argument cdecl frame matches.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.detail: One argument, the result buffer at [E+4], used as the memcpy destination and return value in both.

checks.name: control_flow_shape
checks.detail: Binary Ninja and radare2 agree on 1 blocks / 0 edges (similarity 1.000); angr CFGFast recovers 3 blocks with has_unresolved_jumps=false. The angr block-count difference is a granularity artifact of CFGFast splitting at call returns / rep movsd; the BN and radare2 block and edge tables are identical.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.detail: Retail has no calls: the 6-dword copy is the inlined `rep movsd`. The candidate's memcpy is the same copy; the only BN callee entry is the 0xC35040 memcpy intrinsic.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.detail: The 24-byte stack record, its two undefined words, and the copy to [E+4] match the retail `rep movsd`.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.detail: Both return the [E+4] result buffer pointer.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports "int32_t(int32_t arg1)" at 0x004B8C10; radare2 recovers "fcn.004b8c10 (int32_t arg_1ch);". Both tools place the entry at 0x004B8C10 and agree on the stack/register word count and cleanup; the difference is the level of type/argument-name detail, not the call frame. Candidate declaration: int32_t BreakScript(int32_t param_1);.

limitations: No game process was executed; this review is static (live Binary Ninja, radare2 CFG, angr CFGFast) plus the candidate source.

The candidate defines Break_Script while the catalog name is BreakScript; the provenance comment and the .cpp include still say `void Break_Script()` / "Break_Script.h", and only `004B8C10-Break_Script.hpp` exists in the tree.
angr CFGFast splits the block at the `rep movsd` (3 nodes) while BN and radare2 both report one block; this is an angr granularity artifact, not a real branch.
